answer: Probationary Wake Schedule. New identities get a slow pulse: their first N actions are spread over hours by a per-identity timer seeded at registration. Each agent must also meet a comet check—one sustained activity burst that decays unless followed by steady traffic across a knoll of distinct time bins. Sybils pay in elapsed wall-clock time and idle compute: mass-registering k identities costs k × the wake window before any becomes usable, and synchronized bursts get thinned, so parallel clones gain nothing.
